sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.note: Comparative only: section 2.1.3 (p.16) 'Word stress in PNCV was most likely on the penultimate vowel. This is its position in almost all daughter languages for which phonological descriptions exist, where the historic final syllable is intact.' No Duidui-specific stress statement; Duidui is a lexical source only (Wheatley 1992; Matthew and Mark 1973).

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1926. A Comparative Study of the Melanesian Island Languages. Cambridge: CUP. pp. 418-419 'Lepers' Island' (Rosetta Project excerpt).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.7.25)
sources.note: Silent on stress; bibliographic and dialect note only (Walurigi g vs. k; 'the locale of Nduindui is not specified' for the Hagen & Pineau list). Full 1926 text not open on archive.org (1978 reprint is lending-only).

sources.citation: Codrington, R. H. 1885. The Melanesian Languages. Oxford: Clarendon Press. Section 17 'Oba, Lepers' Island', pp. 420-431.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes the Walurigi dialect of the northern face of the island (= North-East Ambae, east2443), not West Ambae ('The language of the southern face of the island is different'); the alphabet section has no accent statement in any case.

sources.citation: Aru, Carol Cecilia. 2015. A short grammar of Duidui: A language of West Ambae in Northern Vanuatu. MA thesis, The University of the South Pacific. xvii+209 leaves.

sources.note: The only first-hand grammar of the language (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a grammar sketch); a 209-page MA grammar almost certainly has a phonology chapter with a stress statement; source of Wikipedia's phoneme tables.

sources.citation: Hagen, A. & A. Pineau. 1888. Les Nouvelles-Hebrides: etudes ethnographiques. Revue d'Ethnographie 7: 302-362 (Ambae vocabulary pp. 308-319).
